newsitem.title: SPAIN: ATHLETICS-NEBIOLO AIMS TO BAN CONFLICTING MARATHONS.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-NEBIOLO AIMS TO BAN CONFLICTING MARATHONS.

text.p: The president of the International Amateur Athletic Federation said on Saturday he intended to ban competitions which conflicted with IAAF-organised events.

Speaking before Sunday's world half-marathon here, Primo Nebiolo said: "From next year we will protect our events much more strongly. This is the last time there will be competitions on the same day as an IAAF world championship.
"All competitions must have special permits and the IAAF will not give any permit to any event in competition with our events."
The announcement is likely to upset organisers of some well-known independent city marathons, but Nebiolo added:

"We have the strength to control the sport and will disqualify any athletes taking part in other events. We will put a window three or four days before and afterwards when there cannot be any events. We can do what we want because we are the governing body."
Nebiolo's comments were prompted by the fact that many of the world's top road runners have decided to stay away from Sunday's world half-marathon.

Kenya's Paul Tergat, the holder of the world best for the half marathon, will compete over the same distance in Luxembourg while the Berlin Marathon has attracted the likes of Spain's Abel Anton and Kenya's Sammy Lelei.
The IAAF road running commission and the Association of International Marathons are due to meet in Dublin on October 10 but Saturday's announcement will increase the strain between the bodies.
The 1997 World Half Marathon Championships are scheduled for October 4 in Kosice, Poland.
